claims.text: The selected alloy is equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
The as-cast CrMnFeCoNi starting state is strain-free and defect-free.
The as-cast CrMnFeCoNi starting state does not exhibit superconductivity in the tested low-temperature regime.
Approximately 50% cold rolling followed by annealing at 350°C for 1 hour will increase and stabilize the dislocation density.
The intervention will produce strain-induced electronic inhomogeneities.
A high dislocation density locally modifies the electronic density of states in CrMnFeCoNi.
A high dislocation density enhances local electron–phonon coupling in CrMnFeCoNi.
Enhanced local electron–phonon coupling facilitates Cooper-pair formation along dislocation networks.
Cooper-pair formation along dislocation networks can produce filamentary superconductivity in high-defect-density regions.
Cold-rolled and annealed samples will exhibit a superconducting transition between 10 K and 0.3 K.
The proposed superconducting transition will be detectable through zero resistivity and a diamagnetic response.
The untreated as-cast control will remain non-superconducting over the measurement range.
Reducing the dislocation density through recrystallization will diminish or eliminate the superconducting signature.
The proposed effect is limited to a dislocation-density range that enhances electron–phonon coupling without preventing superconducting percolation through excessive inhomogeneity.
The effect is expected under approximately 50% cold rolling and annealing at 350°C for 1 hour but may not extend beyond those processing conditions.
Failure to observe an association between dislocation density and superconducting signatures would falsify the proposed defect-mediated mechanism.
Persistence of superconductivity after recrystallization reduces the dislocation density would falsify the proposed defect-mediated mechanism.
